messages:
mira: Heads-up — noticed our async python client (0.11.2) causing a lot of socket TIME_WAIT on prod after a recent burst test. CPU ok but ephemeral sockets accumulate and we hit file descriptor limits.

mira: Repro is a simple aiohttp loop creating many short-lived clients in tasks. After ~5k requests we see thousands of sockets in TIME_WAIT.

mira: Minimal repro:
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def hit(i):
    async with AsyncClient(api_key="redacted") as c:
        await c.generate("hello")

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(*[hit(i) for i in range(5000)])

asyncio.run(main())
```

mira: Observed behavior: sockets leak even when using async context manager, causing OOM on fd open.

jake: hmm. Are you using uvloop or default loop?

mira: uvloop 0.17.0 on prod. Locally with default loop I see fewer sockets but still higher than expected.

aditya: can you paste netstat or ss output?

mira: snippet:
```
tcp   0  0 10.0.1.5:57238 13.107.21.200:443 TIME_WAIT
tcp   0  0 10.0.1.5:57240 13.107.21.200:443 TIME_WAIT
... (2000 lines)
```

mira: Also saw this log from client: "Unclosed client session" in worker logs intermittently. But code uses async with.

sasha: that sounds like __aenter__/__aexit__ not closing underlying aiohttp connector in some race with cancellation. We had a similar issue with old requests adapter.

aditya: possible causes: (1) task cancellation during __aexit__ skipping close, (2) connector pool default size=0? (3) missing explicit force_close on session.

mira: one more note — dialing high concurrency (~1000 parallel tasks) we see more leakage than low concurrency. So probably a concurrency race.

jake: can you try calling AsyncClient.close() explicitly in finally block to confirm?

mira: tried:
```py
client = AsyncClient()
try:
    await client.generate(...)
finally:
    await client.close()
```
That reduced but didn't eliminate TIME_WAIT.

aditya: interesting. Might be we open ephemeral TCP connections per request because connector is using force_close or disable_keepalive for TLS workaround. Check AsyncClient init args — do we set disable_keepalive when retriable errors happen?

mira: Not intentionally. We do see in telemetry that keepalive is sometimes disabled after certain error codes (429, 503) due to backoff code mutating connector options.

sasha: that's a bug then — mutating connector at runtime can cause connector replacement which might leak sockets until GC. Also if __del__ is relied on for closing, GC won't run deterministically under uvloop high concurrency.

aditya: short-term mitigation: add explicit connection_pool_max and idle_timeout config options on AsyncClient constructor and make them default to conservative values (pool_size=100, idle_timeout=20s). Longer term: ensure AsyncClient exposes a reuseable connector object that isn't swapped without closing previous instance. Also add an explicit .aclose() and document usage pattern.

mira: filed a quick workaround in prod — set session_pool=100 and call close() in finally. Reduced fd leak rate by ~90% but still suspect a small leak during cancellation.

jake: can you share a small trace where task is cancelled mid-request? Might be a missing shield() around __aexit__ or missing try/except around cancellation.

mira: will capture. Also behaviour differs when using SDK with typed stub vs raw client. With typed client (AutoClient) the context manager is a wrapper that wasn't awaiting inner aclose in our version. Could be different codepaths.

sasha: action items: (1) devex to add integration test that spins up a local echo server and runs 5k concurrent short-lived async clients, assert fd usage stable; (2) runtime to add guard to always await connector.close() even on CancelledError; (3) SDK: expose pool_size and idle_timeout and document pattern for long-running loops; (4) add linter warning for creating one-off clients in hot loops.

aditya: assigning to me to implement the forced close and add tests. jake can you own docs + changelog note + new config keys? sasha can you add the linter rule and example in devex recipes?

jake: yep. I'll add a new sample under examples/async_reuse.py showing reuse pattern and the correct try/finally to close. Also add typing note — AsyncClient.__aenter__/__aexit__ should be typed as returning AsyncClient not Any.

mira: awesome. Also feature request: can we add an optional ClientFactory that reuses a single connector across many client instantiations so users who accidentally create many clients still benefit from keepalive?

aditya: good idea. We'll implement factory + a global weakref cache keyed by (pool_size, ssl_context) and ensure explicit close is still required to avoid surprise resource retention.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued for backend/async-client-fixes branch — CI passed for unit tests.

sasha: quick follow-up: please add a regression test that simulates cancellation (asyncio.CancelledError) during __aexit__ to verify connector closed.

mira: thanks all. keeping this thread for notes — will rerun burst test once patch hits staging and report results here. :raised_hands:
